classification.difficultyReason: The supplied diagram already shows the perpendicular journey legs and direct return distance, leaving a straightforward hypotenuse calculation.

content.prompt: John starts at a point $A$ and cycles 12 km due north. He turns east at point $B$, cycles 16 km and reaches point $C$. How far is he from his starting point?

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise question 3, diagram beneath the stem
spec.description: Triangle ABC with A below B and C east of B; right angle at B. A separate upward north arrow with a horizontal crossbar sits to the left. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB = 12 km, BC = 16 km, angle ABC = 90 degrees; AC is the unknown direct distance.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths and point names are visible; AC has no supplied answer.

answer.worked:
North and east are perpendicular, so $AC$ is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=12^2+16^2\\AC^2&=144+256\\AC^2&=400\\AC&=\sqrt{400}\\AC&=20\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
John is 20 km from his starting point.
